label: read2-bm-contract
in_my_words: Someone wants to offer a London design studio a small printed plastic strip that curls in damp air, which could open or close a window shade without a motor. They would also offer a maths rule, checked by software, saying how far such a strip can curl at most. They did background research first and concluded the strip probably can't be used on tall English flats because of fire rules, and that nobody pays for a design rule alone.
how_in_my_words: Helpers read building fire rules, printer-maker data, safety sheets, grant lists and patents, and saved quotes from what they read. A second set of readers rechecked the main claims, and only confirmed claims were kept. They compared how much the strip bends from heat versus damp, and re-ran key sums. They also wrote down a bet beforehand about what they would find, so they could see if they were wrong. Nothing has been built or tested yet.

test_questions.question: Why can't the printed shade probably go on tall flats in England?
test_questions.my_answer: Above about 18 metres, outer wall parts must be nearly non-burning, shading slats included, and a desk print can't be fire-graded.

test_questions.question: What does the design rule say?
test_questions.my_answer: The curl can never exceed 1.5 times the layer size mismatch divided by thickness.

test_questions.question: Does Lean prove a real printed strip will curl as predicted?
test_questions.my_answer: No, it only checks the maths of the model; real strips must be measured.

test_questions.question: How much will the sample cost to make?
test_questions.my_answer: Unknown; only a 250 pound minimum budget is listed.

test_questions.question: Who is the team making the offer?
test_questions.my_answer: The text doesn't know; company or university is undecided.

sentences_i_could_not_follow: Its first and widest sentence is narrower than first thought.
The swelling figure for one bendy resin came from a scrambled data sheet.
The studio prints with robot arms and plant-based plastic, not with resin or powder. So our samples only prove the shape idea, not a finished product.
Singapore 0.98 (shade mostly open in hours when shade is wanted), Madrid 0.95, Houston 0.38.
what_would_help: Open with one plain paragraph saying what the offer is and what the verdict is. Say who the research is for and why a studio would care. Explain the 1.5 rule with a tiny worked example. Cut the jargon (grants, patent terms, resin names) or explain it where it first appears. Explain what 'scrambled data sheet' means. Resolve the odd mismatch: the studio doesn't print resin, yet most of the checks are about resin. Put the 'check yourself' commands in a separate technical appendix.
